answer.rationale: With the primary contract expiring in 14 days and the line already at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, switching vendors now (memory_c2) carries unacceptable onboarding/delivery risk despite its cost appeal, and deferring (memory_c5) isn't viable since this is a critical, expiring contract. Memory_c4 shows that renegotiating at renewal has historically recovered real margin via benchmarking, and memory_c1/c6 confirm incumbent continuity preserves delivery stability while multi-year terms can still cut unit cost. Negotiating terms with the incumbent at renewal directly targets the 18% cost mandate while keeping the proven-stable supply chain intact, minimizing delivery risk. I verified c4 to confirm the negotiation outcome was real margin recovery and not just a one-off anecdote, and c2 to check whether switching vendor risk was overstated given the tight 14-day window — if onboarding was truly fast and clean, that could change the calculus for next cycle even though it's too risky to execute now.
